headline: The US nuclear regulator has approved the Tennessee Valley Authority's plan to build a 300-megawatt small modular reactor in Tennessee, the first of its design cleared for construction in the country.
score_reason: Pool 6 lowered by 2: the permit was issued on 29 Sep 2026 and widely reported on 30 Sep and 1 Oct; this 6 Oct piece adds only background.
importance_line: The approval is a step toward smaller reactors that utilities and data center builders hope can supply steady power, which could matter to electricity customers in the Tennessee Valley, but the permit does not allow operation, no start date or cost is set, and the savings are unproven.
summary: TechRadar reports that the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission has approved a construction permit for the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA), the federal power utility, to build a GE Vernova Hitachi BWRX-300 at its Clinch River site, a small modular reactor (a compact design built with more factory-made parts) rated at 300 megawatts, about a quarter of the size of the newest reactors at Georgia's Vogtle plant; the permit was issued on 29 Sep 2026, according to Power Engineering, a week before TechRadar's report. TVA still needs a separate license before it can load fuel or generate power and has not set a construction date, and TechRadar notes that the hoped-for savings from repeating one design remain unproven in the US.
notes: Older news re-dated into the window: the NRC permit was issued on Tuesday 29 Sep 2026 (Power Engineering, 1 Oct) and reported on 30 Sep and 1 Oct by Neutron Bytes, NEI Magazine and others; TechRadar's 6 Oct article is a feature. It is not in our earlier reports or in the last four pools, but the editor may hold it as old news. The UK, Canada and Texas plans are TechRadar's background, not new events.
